source.text: The lowest of the slices' hottest cells: the end slice (index 0), which makes the least heat. Slice 0 of 9 (centre at 0.0212 m, heat rate 1.364 kW/m, coolant 589.67 K): the closed-form series solution of that slice gives 639.8047 K at the centre. The power shape is a cosine, normalised to an average of 1, with the coolant read from the table at each slice's centre (linear between the two points). The solver's slices exchange a little heat along the height, which this solution does not have, so the tolerance is the sum of: the mesh bound 5 x 36.18 K / 100^2 = 0.018 K; the axial conduction allowance 3 x 0.00099 (the estimate as a fraction of the largest rise) x 288.7 K (the largest rise of any slice above its coolant) = 0.854 K; the cosine's 41-point table, 1e-3 of the slice's rise of 50.1 K = 0.05 K; rounded up to 0.05 K (0.95 K), fixed before any run.
source.check: Second method: FEED's own per-slice closed form (src/core/closedForm.ts through axialSummary, tests/seedOracleStack.test.ts, to 1e-3 K apart from the cosine's table term), and the real solver (FEED_SOLVER=1): every check of the run passes and the solver's slice peaks are inside the tolerances.

coverage.domain: synthetic pin as 9 radial slices over 0.381 m with a cosine power shape, 5 kW/m on average (7.9 kW/m at the peak), a coolant table that warms linearly from 573 K at the bottom to 873 K at the top (a sodium-like rise; film coefficient 30000 W/m2/K)
